text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Attorney-General Amos Wako hints that a number of leading personalities implicated in the misappropriation of public funds may not be prosecuted.
- Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani ends four-day visit to Kenya with the signing of a joint agreement which touches on global politics and economies of the two nations.

- Ruling Kenya African National Union party secretary-general Joseph Kamotho dismisses the government authority structure proposed by the opposition alliance as a "political trick, whose intention is to create jobs for the boys (opposition leaders)."
- President Danel arap Moi says issues affecting different communities should not be debated through the media as this often leads to misinterpretation of facts.
- Motor vehicle dealers have complained over alleged inefficiency and poor services at the department now concerned with vehicle registration at the Kenya Revenue Authority.
- Police launch investigations into claims that millions of shillings belonging to Mumias Out-Growers Sugar Company was banked in personal accounts.

- The chairman of the opposition party Kenya National Democratic Alliance Mukaru Ng'ang'a laments that opposition leaders are sidelining him and have never invited him or informed him of any alliance meetings.

- The belated acquisition of the recently-revived Heritage Bank by the Central Bank of Kenya precipitates what could be another banking crisis arising from the political manipulation of small banks, by coterie of politicians and business executives favoured by the KANU government.
